notes: The 10-year US interest rate (4.91%) is 0.79% above the 3-month rate (4.12%), but the gap has shrunk by 0.21% in 3 months: a shrinking gap often comes late in an expansion.
Copper has gained 11.1% on gold over 3 months. Copper follows factory and building demand, while gold is bought in worrying times, so this points to stronger growth.
Fear gauge (VIX) at 35.9: investors are nervous (over 25 = stressed).
The US stock market (S&P 500) is below its 200-day (about 10-month) average price: a broad downtrend.

todaysConditions.note: The US dollar has risen 4.9% against major currencies over 3 months. Gains made abroad shrink when converted back to dollars, and countries that borrowed in dollars find the debt harder to repay.
Copper, a gauge of demand for industrial metals, is down 17% over 3 months: bad for markets full of mining companies.

The fear gauge (VIX) is high 35.9 (over 25 = stressed), and world stocks are 7.0% below their 200-day (about 10-month) average. Steadier markets then tend to hold up better, and emerging markets suffer most.
Chip-maker shares did 15.8% worse than world stocks over 3 months: a drag on tech-heavy markets.
